title: Hole Quality and Multi-Objective Optimisation in Dry Drilling of GLARE 3-3/2 Fibre Metal Laminates with HSS and Carbide Drills
content: Dry drilling of autoclave-cured GLARE 3-3/2 laminates was investigated with rolled and ground high-speed-steel drills (HSS-R, HSS-G) and a carbide-tipped drill in a 3³ full factorial design (715, 1520 and 3030 rpm; 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 mm/rev). Thrust force, infrared temperatures and the non-contact topography of the entry and exit faces were recorded for every hole, and sectioned hole walls were examined by scanning electron microscopy. Drill type governed the thrust force (29.6% contribution; 33.3 N for HSS-G versus 39.5 N for carbide), whereas feed governed the maximum drill temperature (38%; 101.5–114.6 °C); workpiece temperatures stayed below 43 °C, so thermal damage of the epoxy layers can be excluded. Exit burrs dominated over entry damage (mean burr height −3.9 μm at entry versus +25.7 μm at exit; p < 0.001). The carbide drill produced the most accurate holes but the largest exit burrs (up to 152 μm), the HSS-R drill produced bell-mouthed entries (+0.30 mm), and the HSS-G drill produced the flattest edges. Hole walls showed fibre pull-out, matrix chipping and interfacial debonding with HSS-R but transverse fibre shearing with carbide. Contribution analysis of 81 replicated measurements showed that exit-edge quality is governed by drill-specific speed–feed interactions. Response-surface modelling with a weighted desirability function and exhaustive grid search identified HSS-G at 1520 rpm and 0.2 mm/rev as the best compromise (D = 0.867; thrust force 31.1 N; exit burr height 1.8 μm; bulging ratio 0.8%).
